item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 20. Building Yocto 6.0 Wrynose for the Beaglebone Black
item.description: It has been a full year since I posted my first article about building Yocto for the Beaglebone Black. At first I used Kirkstone, then updated to Scarthgap and thought that would last quite a while :vv, but Wrynose brings fairly big structural changes. So I am writing this extra post on how to build with the new version; I think from 6.0 onwards the structure will stay the same.

item.description:

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 18. GDB debugging through recipe-sysroot
item.description:
In this post I show you how to debug a binary built by a recipe using the recipe-sysroot in that recipe's output folder.

1. What is a sysroot?

Sysroot means system root: a folder acting as a virtual root filesystem for cross-compiling. It contains the header files, libraries and artifacts the compiler/linker needs to build code for the target without running on the target.

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 17. Installing Links-X11, browsing the web on core-image-sato
item.description: The other day I installed Android 6 on the Beaglebone Black and saw a Browser app, but it could not browse the web. Newer boards such as the FRDM i.MX93 support Chromium well, but that certainly requires much better hardware.

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 15. Changing the Boot Logo
item.description: Okay, in this post I show how to change the Boot Logo on the Beaglebone Black. At first I thought it would require deep research, but in reality changing it is quite simple. That is one of the nice things about Linux: there is support for so many Packages. My job is to find what I need and put it together.

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 14. X11 and RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol)
item.description:
Since building Weston was far too complicated, and I also tried Weston + RDP without success, I switched to X11 + RDP to keep things simpler

1. Why use RDP

The goal of using RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is that you can access the board remotely with a graphical interface, like VNC.

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 13. Building Weston, fixing input and dnd errors
item.description: When I started, I did not expect to write this post; I thought I would go straight to the RDP + Weston post. Because on the STM32MP157 it built right away, but on this Beaglebone Black it took me 2 days to get Weston working more or less properly.

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 12. Transferring files over TFTP
item.description:
In the previous post I showed you how to transfer files over UART; in this post I show you how to transfer files over TFTP. (u-boot supports TFTP for loading files)

1. What is TFTP?

TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) is a very simple file transfer protocol running over UDP (port 69).

item.title: [Yocto-BBB] 10. Booting from eMMC
item.description:
In this post I show you how to configure the Beaglebone Black to boot from eMMC.

1. Why

1.1 What is eMMC?

eMMC (embedded MultiMediaCard) is a type of integrated storage that combines NAND flash and a controller on the same chip.
